| [LIT-230](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-230.md) | Riesz representation theorem (Wikipedia) | Wikipedia contributors (2026), <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riesz_representation_theorem>. A Hilbert space is isometrically (anti-)isomorphic to its continuous dual — every continuous linear functional φ is x ↦ ⟨x, f_φ⟩ for a unique f_φ with ‖f_φ‖ = ‖φ‖ — and this identification is what defines adjoints and the bra–ket correspondence. | Deferred — seeded from the abstract and a skim on 2026-09-26; not read in full |
| [LIT-237](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-237.md) | Bra–ket notation (Wikipedia) | Wikipedia contributors (2026), <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bra%E2%80%93ket_notation>. Dirac's bra–ket notation writes vectors as kets and continuous linear functionals as bras, and on a Hilbert space the Riesz representation theorem is what licenses treating every bra as the conjugate of a ket, so that ⟨φ\|ψ⟩ is at once a functional applied to a vector and an inner product. | Deferred — seeded from the abstract and a skim on 2026-09-26; not read in full |
